source.text: וַיְהִ֤י הַגּוֹרָל֙ לְמַטֵּ֣ה מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה כִּי־ה֖וּא בְּכ֣וֹר יוֹסֵ֑ף לְמָכִיר֩ בְּכ֨וֹר מְנַשֶּׁ֜ה אֲבִ֣י הַגִּלְעָ֗ד כִּ֣י ה֤וּא הָיָה֙ אִ֣ישׁ מִלְחָמָ֔ה וַֽיְהִי־ל֖וֹ הַגִּלְעָ֥ד וְהַבָּשָֽׁן׃

records.literal_gloss: And was the lot for [the] tribe of Manasseh, for he [was the] firstborn of Joseph; for Machir, [the] firstborn of Manasseh, [the] father of the Gilead, because he was a man of war, and were to him the Gilead and the Bashan.

en.L: And the lot was for the tribe of Manasseh, for he [was] the firstborn of Joseph. For Machir, the firstborn of Manasseh, the father of Gilead, because he was a man of war, Gilead and Bashan were his.
en.B: This was the land that came by lot to the tribe of Manasseh, for he was Joseph's firstborn. Machir, Manasseh's firstborn and the father of Gilead, had Gilead and Bashan, because he was a warrior.
en.R: Next, land was given by lot to the tribe of Manasseh, Joseph's oldest son. Manasseh's oldest son Machir was the father of Gilead. Machir was a strong fighter, so he had already been given the lands of Gilead and Bashan, east of the Jordan River.

decisions.choice: the lot: the share of land decided by casting lots
decisions.reason: The land west of the Jordan was shared out among the tribes by lot, so that the LORD, not the leaders, decided each tribe's place (Numbers 26:52-56; 33:54; Joshua 14:1-2). The word "lot" can mean both the object cast and the share it gave; here it is the share. Joshua 16:1 opens the lot of Joseph's descendants, and this verse turns to the part of it that fell to Manasseh.

decisions.choice: the firstborn of Joseph: Manasseh was Joseph's elder son
decisions.reason: Manasseh was born before Ephraim (Genesis 41:51-52), though Jacob gave the younger son the greater blessing (Genesis 48:13-20), and Ephraim's share is described first (Joshua 16:5-10). The verse gives Manasseh's birthright as the reason he too receives a full share, beside the land already given east of the Jordan.

decisions.choice: Machir received Gilead and Bashan: the land east of the Jordan, given earlier
decisions.reason: Machir's clan had taken Gilead, and Moses gave it to them (Numbers 32:39-40; Deuteronomy 3:13-15; Joshua 13:29-31). Bashan was the land north of Gilead, east of the Sea of Chinnereth. The verse recalls that gift and gives the reason for it: Machir was a fighting man. The lot described in the rest of the chapter is for the other clans, west of the Jordan (verse 2).

decisions.choice: the father of Gilead: Gilead is both a man and a land
decisions.reason: Gilead was Machir's son (Numbers 26:29), and the region east of the Jordan bore the same name. In this verse "Gilead" first names the man, then the land.

decisions.choice: a warrior / a strong fighter
decisions.reason: "A man of war" means a fighting man, a warrior; Balanced and Readable say so in one word or phrase. Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase.

decisions.choice: had already been given ... east of the Jordan River
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that this gift was made before the lot (m3) and where the land lay, as verse 5 says. Literal and Balanced leave it to the reader.

source.text: וַ֠יְהִי לִבְנֵ֨י מְנַשֶּׁ֥ה הַנּוֹתָרִים֮ לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם֒ לִבְנֵ֨י אֲבִיעֶ֜זֶר וְלִבְנֵי־חֵ֗לֶק וְלִבְנֵ֤י אַשְׂרִיאֵל֙ וְלִבְנֵי־שֶׁ֔כֶם וְלִבְנֵי־חֵ֖פֶר וְלִבְנֵ֣י שְׁמִידָ֑ע אֵ֠לֶּה בְּנֵ֨י מְנַשֶּׁ֧ה בֶּן־יוֹסֵ֛ף הַזְּכָרִ֖ים לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And was [the lot] for [the] sons of Manasseh the remaining by their clans: for [the] sons of Abiezer and for [the] sons of Helek and for [the] sons of Asriel and for [the] sons of Shechem and for [the] sons of Hepher and for [the] sons of Shemida; these [are the] sons of Manasseh son of Joseph, the males, by their clans.

en.L: And [the lot] was for the rest of the {{gender:descendants|sons}} of Manasseh by their clans: for the {{gender:descendants|sons}} of Abiezer and for the {{gender:descendants|sons}} of Helek and for the {{gender:descendants|sons}} of Asriel and for the {{gender:descendants|sons}} of Shechem and for the {{gender:descendants|sons}} of Hepher and for the {{gender:descendants|sons}} of Shemida. These [were] the sons of Manasseh son of Joseph, the males, by their clans.
en.B: The lot was also for the rest of Manasseh's descendants, clan by clan: the clans of Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Hepher and Shemida. These were the male descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph, listed by their clans.
en.R: The rest of Manasseh's descendants also received land by lot, one share for each clan. The clans were named after Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Hepher and Shemida. These were the clans of Manasseh, Joseph's son, counted through the men of each family.

decisions.choice: Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Hepher, Shemida: the six clans of Gilead
decisions.reason: These are the clans descended from Gilead son of Machir in the census of Numbers 26:30-32, where Abiezer is called by the short form Iezer. They are the clans that settle west of the Jordan. Gideon later came from the clan of Abiezer (Judges 6:11, 34), and Shechem is also the name of a town in Manasseh's hill country (verse 7).

decisions.choice: the rest of the descendants of Manasseh: those who had no land yet
decisions.reason: "The rest" are the clans not already given land with Machir east of the Jordan (verse 1). The same word comes back in verse 6.

decisions.choice: the males: the clans counted through their men
decisions.reason: The list ends by saying these were "the males", the sons through whom each clan's line was traced. It prepares for verse 3, where one man of the clan of Hepher had no sons, only daughters, and yet his line received land.

decisions.choice: descendants (clans) / sons, the males
decisions.reason: The "sons" of each clan are the clan's people, so Literal gives "descendants" with "sons" as the traditional form, and Balanced and Readable name the clans. In the last sentence the verse itself says "the males", so every level keeps a male word there and no inclusive form is offered.

source.text: וְלִצְלָפְחָד֩ בֶּן־חֵ֨פֶר בֶּן־גִּלְעָ֜ד בֶּן־מָכִ֣יר בֶּן־מְנַשֶּׁ֗ה לֹא־הָ֥יוּ ל֛וֹ בָּנִ֖ים כִּ֣י אִם־בָּנ֑וֹת וְאֵ֨לֶּה֙ שְׁמ֣וֹת בְּנֹתָ֔יו מַחְלָ֣ה וְנֹעָ֔ה חָגְלָ֥ה מִלְכָּ֖ה וְתִרְצָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And to Zelophehad son of Hepher son of Gilead son of Machir son of Manasseh not were to him sons, but only daughters; and these [are the] names of his daughters: Mahlah and Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah.

en.L: But Zelophehad son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, had no sons, only daughters; and these [are] the names of his daughters: Mahlah and Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah.
en.B: But Zelophehad son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, had no sons, only daughters. His daughters were named Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah.
en.R: But Zelophehad had no sons. He had only daughters. He was the son of Hepher, and Hepher was a descendant of Gilead, Machir and Manasseh. Zelophehad's daughters were named Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah.

decisions.choice: Zelophehad had no sons, only daughters: the case settled in Numbers 27 and 36
decisions.reason: The census named Zelophehad's five daughters (Numbers 26:33). They asked Moses for their father's share, and the LORD ruled that it should pass to them (Numbers 27:1-11); later he ruled that they must marry within their father's tribe, so the land would stay in Manasseh (Numbers 36:1-12). Verses 3-6 tell how that ruling was carried out when the land was shared.

decisions.choice: but only daughters
decisions.reason: As in Numbers 26:33, the words "but if" after a negative mean "only": he had daughters and no sons.

decisions.choice: Noah: a woman's name, not the Noah of the flood
decisions.reason: As in Numbers 26:33, this name is spelled differently in Hebrew from the name of Noah in Genesis 6-9.

decisions.choice: Mahlah and Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah (L); the names as in Numbers 26:33 and 27:1
decisions.reason: The names are given in the same order as in Numbers 26:33 and 27:1, with the same joining words at Literal; Readable traces the family line as Numbers 27:1 does.

source.text: וַתִּקְרַ֡בְנָה לִפְנֵי֩ אֶלְעָזָ֨ר הַכֹּהֵ֜ן וְלִפְנֵ֣י׀יְהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ בִּן־נ֗וּן וְלִפְנֵ֤י הַנְּשִׂיאִים֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יְהוָה֙ צִוָּ֣ה אֶת־מֹשֶׁ֔ה לָֽתֶת־לָ֥נוּ נַחֲלָ֖ה בְּת֣וֹךְ אַחֵ֑ינוּ וַיִּתֵּ֨ן לָהֶ֜ם אֶל־פִּ֤י יְהוָה֙ נַֽחֲלָ֔ה בְּת֖וֹךְ אֲחֵ֥י אֲבִיהֶֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And they drew near before Eleazar the priest and before Joshua son of Nun and before the leaders, saying, Yahweh commanded Moses to give to us an inheritance in [the] midst of our brothers; and he gave to them, at [the] mouth of Yahweh, an inheritance in [the] midst of [the] brothers of their father.

en.L: And they drew near before Eleazar the priest and before Joshua son of Nun and before the leaders, saying, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our brothers." And he gave them, at the mouth of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, an inheritance among the brothers of their father.
en.B: They came forward before Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun and the leaders. "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} commanded Moses," they said, "to give us an inheritance among our relatives." So Joshua gave them an inheritance among their father's brothers, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded.
en.R: They went to Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun and the leaders. They said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} commanded Moses to give us land of our own among our relatives." So Joshua did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded. He gave them land among their father's relatives.

decisions.choice: the LORD commanded Moses: the ruling of Numbers 27:6-7
decisions.reason: The daughters remind the leaders of the LORD's words to Moses: "You shall surely give them a possession of inheritance among the brothers of their father" (Numbers 27:7). Moses had died, so they bring the ruling to those now sharing out the land: Eleazar, Joshua and the tribal leaders, the very people named for that task (Numbers 34:17-18; Joshua 14:1).

decisions.choice: among our brothers: among the men of our clan
decisions.reason: "Brothers" here are kinsmen, the male relatives of their clan, as in Numbers 27:4, 7. The daughters ask to hold land beside their father's brothers, in their father's place.

decisions.choice: he gave them: Joshua, acting for the leaders
decisions.reason: The verb is singular and has no named subject. Joshua is the one who carries out the sharing of the land in these chapters (14:13; 15:13), so he is the most likely subject; the priest and the leaders act with him.

decisions.choice: at the mouth of the LORD: by the LORD's command
decisions.reason: "Mouth" stands for what someone says. The phrase means that the gift was made just as the LORD had ordered, as in Numbers 9:18 and 33:2.

decisions.choice: Joshua
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Joshua as the one who gave the land (m3); Literal keeps "he".

decisions.choice: our relatives; their father's brothers (B) / relatives (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced says "relatives" for the daughters' own words, since they mean their kinsmen, and keeps "their father's brothers" in the narrator's words, as in Numbers 27:7. Readable says "relatives" for both, and "land of our own" for the inheritance, as Numbers 27:4 does.

source.text: וַיִּפְּל֥וּ חַבְלֵֽי־מְנַשֶּׁ֖ה עֲשָׂרָ֑ה לְבַ֞ד מֵאֶ֤רֶץ הַגִּלְעָד֙ וְהַבָּשָׁ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֖ר מֵעֵ֥בֶר לַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And fell [the] portions of Manasseh ten, apart from [the] land of the Gilead and the Bashan which [is] from [the] other side of the Jordan,

en.L: And ten portions fell to Manasseh, apart from the land of Gilead and Bashan, which [is] across the Jordan,
en.B: So ten shares fell to Manasseh, besides the land of Gilead and Bashan across the Jordan,
en.R: So Manasseh received ten shares of land west of the Jordan River. This was in addition to Gilead and Bashan on the east side of the river.

decisions.choice: portions fell: shares of land came by lot
decisions.reason: The word for "portion" first means a measuring cord, then the piece of land measured out with it. A portion "falls" to someone because it is given by lot, as the lot falls (Psalm 16:6 uses both pictures).

decisions.choice: ten portions: five clans and five daughters
decisions.reason: Six clans are named in verse 2. Hepher's line passed to Zelophehad, who had no sons, so his share went to his five daughters. The five other clans and the five daughters make ten shares, which verse 6 explains. This is the most natural way to count them; the text does not list the ten.

decisions.choice: across the Jordan: east of the river
decisions.reason: The phrase means "on the other side of the Jordan". Joshua is speaking from the land west of the river, so it means the east side, where Gilead and Bashan lay (verse 1; 13:29-31).

decisions.choice: west of the Jordan River ... on the east side of the river
decisions.reason: Readable says where each part of Manasseh's land lay, so the reader can see that the ten shares were in addition to the land east of the Jordan. It ends its sentence here, while Literal and Balanced run on into verse 6.

source.text: כִּ֚י בְּנ֣וֹת מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה נָחֲל֥וּ נַחֲלָ֖ה בְּת֣וֹךְ בָּנָ֑יו וְאֶ֨רֶץ֙ הַגִּלְעָ֔ד הָיְתָ֥ה לִבְנֵֽי־מְנַשֶּׁ֖ה הַנּֽוֹתָרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: for [the] daughters of Manasseh inherited an inheritance in [the] midst of his sons; and [the] land of the Gilead was for [the] sons of Manasseh the remaining.

en.L: for the daughters of Manasseh inherited an inheritance among his sons; and the land of Gilead belonged to the rest of the {{gender:descendants|sons}} of Manasseh.
en.B: because the daughters of Manasseh received an inheritance along with his sons. The land of Gilead belonged to the rest of Manasseh's descendants.
en.R: That was because the women from Manasseh's family line, Zelophehad's daughters, received land along with the men. The land of Gilead went to the rest of Manasseh's descendants.

decisions.choice: the daughters of Manasseh ... his sons: his female and male descendants
decisions.reason: "Daughters" and "sons" here mean descendants, as "sons of Israel" means Israelites. The daughters are Zelophehad's five daughters (verse 3), set beside the men who led the other clans.

decisions.choice: the rest of the descendants of Manasseh: the clan of Machir
decisions.reason: In verse 2, "the rest" were the clans settling west of the Jordan. Here "the rest" are those not just named, the people of Machir, who had Gilead east of the river (verse 1). The word points to whichever group has not yet been mentioned.

decisions.choice: the women from Manasseh's family line, Zelophehad's daughters
decisions.reason: Readable names the daughters of verse 3, so that "daughters of Manasseh" is not taken to mean Manasseh's own children.

source.text: וַיְהִ֤י גְבוּל־מְנַשֶּׁה֙ מֵֽאָשֵׁ֔ר הַֽמִּכְמְתָ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־פְּנֵ֣י שְׁכֶ֑ם וְהָלַ֤ךְ הַגְּבוּל֙ אֶל־הַיָּמִ֔ין אֶל־יֹשְׁבֵ֖י עֵ֥ין תַּפּֽוּחַ׃

records.literal_gloss: And was [the] border of Manasseh from Asher [to] the Michmethath which [is] on [the] face of Shechem, and went the border to the right, to [the] inhabitants of En-tappuah.

en.L: And the border of Manasseh was from Asher to Michmethath, which [is] facing Shechem; and the border goes to the right, to the inhabitants of En-tappuah.
en.B: The border of Manasseh ran from Asher to Michmethath, east of Shechem. From there the border goes south toward the people of En-tappuah.
en.R: Manasseh's border started at Asher and went to Michmethath, east of the town of Shechem. Then it turned south toward the people who lived in En-tappuah.

decisions.choice: Asher: here probably a place, not the tribe
decisions.reason: The border is traced from one point to the next, so Asher here seems to be a town or district on Manasseh's southern edge. The tribe of Asher lay far to the north-west (verse 10; 19:24-31). Its site is not known.

decisions.choice: Michmethath, Shechem, En-tappuah: points on the line between Manasseh and Ephraim
decisions.reason: Michmethath also marks Ephraim's border (16:6). Shechem was the well-known town between Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim (Genesis 12:6; Joshua 24:1). En-tappuah, "spring of Tappuah", was near the town of Tappuah (verse 8; 16:8). The line described here is the same boundary as in 16:5-8, seen from Manasseh's side.

decisions.choice: on the face of: east of, facing
decisions.reason: "On the face of" a place often means in front of it, and since a person faced east to find directions, it can mean east of it (Genesis 23:19). Here it most likely means east of Shechem.

decisions.choice: to the right: south
decisions.reason: Facing east, the right hand is south. The word for "right hand" is used for the south, as in Psalm 89:13.

decisions.choice: east of; south
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the directions plainly (m3, m4); Literal keeps "facing" and "to the right".

source.text: לִמְנַשֶּׁ֕ה הָיְתָ֖ה אֶ֣רֶץ תַּפּ֑וּחַ וְתַפּ֛וּחַ אֶל־גְּב֥וּל מְנַשֶּׁ֖ה לִבְנֵ֥י אֶפְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: To Manasseh was [the] land of Tappuah; and Tappuah, to [the] border of Manasseh, [was] for [the] sons of Ephraim.

en.L: To Manasseh belonged the land of Tappuah; but Tappuah, on the border of Manasseh, [belonged] to the {{gender:descendants|sons}} of Ephraim.
en.B: The land around Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, but the town of Tappuah itself, on Manasseh's border, belonged to the descendants of Ephraim.
en.R: The land around Tappuah belonged to Manasseh. But the town of Tappuah, right on Manasseh's border, belonged to Ephraim's descendants.

decisions.choice: the land of Tappuah and Tappuah: the fields around the town and the town itself
decisions.reason: The verse sets the countryside of Tappuah against the town. The fields were Manasseh's, while the town on the border went to Ephraim. Joshua 16:9 says Ephraim had other towns inside Manasseh's land, and verse 9 here says the same.

decisions.choice: the land around ... the town of Tappuah itself
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "around" and "the town" so that the two uses of the name can be told apart (m1).

source.text: וְיָרַ֣ד הַגְּבוּל֩ נַ֨חַל קָנָ֜ה נֶ֣גְבָּה לַנַּ֗חַל עָרִ֤ים הָאֵ֨לֶּה֙ לְאֶפְרַ֔יִם בְּת֖וֹךְ עָרֵ֣י מְנַשֶּׁ֑ה וּגְב֤וּל מְנַשֶּׁה֙ מִצְּפ֣וֹן לַנַּ֔חַל וַיְהִ֥י תֹצְאֹתָ֖יו הַיָּֽמָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And went down the border [to the] wadi of Kanah, southward to the wadi; these cities [were] to Ephraim in [the] midst of [the] cities of Manasseh; and [the] border of Manasseh [was] from [the] north of the wadi, and were its goings out at the sea.

en.L: And the border goes down to the wadi of Kanah, south of the wadi. These cities [belonged] to Ephraim among the cities of Manasseh; and the border of Manasseh [is] on the north side of the wadi, and its end is at the sea.
en.B: Then the border goes down to the Wadi Kanah. South of the wadi there were towns that belonged to Ephraim, though they lay among the towns of Manasseh. Manasseh's border runs along the north side of the wadi and ends at the sea.
en.R: Then the border went down to the Wadi Kanah, a stream that is dry most of the year. Some towns south of the wadi belonged to Ephraim, even though they were among Manasseh's towns. Manasseh's border ran along the north side of the wadi and ended at the Mediterranean Sea.

decisions.choice: the wadi of Kanah: a stream bed running west to the sea
decisions.reason: A wadi is a valley whose stream flows only in the rainy season. The Wadi Kanah ran west from the hills to the Mediterranean and formed part of the line between Ephraim and Manasseh (16:8).

decisions.choice: these cities: Ephraim's towns south of the wadi, inside Manasseh's land
decisions.reason: The verse does not name "these cities". It most likely refers to towns lying south of the wadi that were given to Ephraim though they stood among Manasseh's towns, as 16:9 says. The Hebrew is brief here, and the exact sense of the clause is not certain.

decisions.choice: its goings out: its end
decisions.reason: As in Numbers 34:4-5, the word means the farthest point a border reaches. The northern line between the two tribes ends at the Mediterranean coast.

decisions.choice: wadi (L), Wadi Kanah (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 16:8, Literal says "wadi" and Balanced and Readable use it as part of the name; Readable explains it and names the sea. Literal and Balanced describe the line in the present tense, as in 15:3.

decisions.choice: towns
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word covers any walled settlement, large or small; Balanced and Readable say "towns", which fits the size of most of these places. Literal keeps "cities".

source.text: נֶ֣גְבָּה לְאֶפְרַ֗יִם וְצָפ֨וֹנָה֙ לִמְנַשֶּׁ֔ה וַיְהִ֥י הַיָּ֖ם גְּבוּל֑וֹ וּבְאָשֵׁר֙ יִפְגְּע֣וּן מִצָּפ֔וֹן וּבְיִשָּׂשכָ֖ר מִמִּזְרָֽח׃

records.literal_gloss: Southward [was] to Ephraim and northward to Manasseh, and was the sea its border; and on Asher they touch from [the] north, and on Issachar from [the] east.

en.L: Southward [it belonged] to Ephraim and northward to Manasseh, and the sea [is] its border; and they touch Asher on the north and Issachar on the east.
en.B: The land to the south belonged to Ephraim and the land to the north to Manasseh, with the sea as its border. Manasseh reaches Asher on the north and Issachar on the east.
en.R: Ephraim had the land to the south, and Manasseh had the land to the north. The sea was Manasseh's western border. On the north its land touched the land of Asher, and on the east the land of Issachar.

decisions.choice: they touch: Manasseh's people, spoken of as many
decisions.reason: The verb is plural, though Manasseh has just been named as one tribe. The tribe is thought of as its people, whose land meets the land of Asher and Issachar. The meaning is not affected.

decisions.choice: Asher and Issachar: the tribes to the north and east
decisions.reason: Here Asher is the tribe, whose land lay along the coast to the north (19:24-31), and Issachar lay to the north-east around the Valley of Jezreel (19:17-23). The verse sums up Manasseh's neighbors on each side.

decisions.choice: the sea was its border: the western edge
decisions.reason: The Mediterranean formed the western side of Manasseh's land, as it did for Judah and Ephraim (15:12; 16:8).

decisions.choice: western border
decisions.reason: Readable says which border the sea formed (m3), which Literal and Balanced leave to the reader.

source.text: וַיְהִ֨י לִמְנַשֶּׁ֜ה בְּיִשָּׂשכָ֣ר וּבְאָשֵׁ֗ר בֵּית־שְׁאָ֣ן וּ֠בְנוֹתֶיהָ וְיִבְלְעָ֨ם וּבְנוֹתֶ֜יהָ וְֽאֶת־יֹשְׁבֵ֧י דֹ֣אר וּבְנוֹתֶ֗יהָ וְיֹשְׁבֵ֤י עֵֽין־דֹּר֙ וּבְנֹתֶ֔יהָ וְיֹשְׁבֵ֤י תַעְנַךְ֙ וּבְנֹתֶ֔יהָ וְיֹשְׁבֵ֥י מְגִדּ֖וֹ וּבְנוֹתֶ֑יהָ שְׁלֹ֖שֶׁת הַנָּֽפֶת׃

records.literal_gloss: And was to Manasseh in Issachar and in Asher Beth-shean and its daughters, and Ibleam and its daughters, and [the] inhabitants of Dor and its daughters, and [the] inhabitants of En-dor and its daughters, and [the] inhabitants of Taanach and its daughters, and [the] inhabitants of Megiddo and its daughters; three [of] the heights.

en.L: And Manasseh had, in Issachar and in Asher, Beth-shean and its villages, and Ibleam and its villages, and the inhabitants of Dor and its villages, and the inhabitants of En-dor and its villages, and the inhabitants of Taanach and its villages, and the inhabitants of Megiddo and its villages: the three of the heights.
en.B: In the land of Issachar and Asher, Manasseh also had Beth-shean, Ibleam, and the people of Dor, En-dor, Taanach and Megiddo, each with its villages: the three hill districts.
en.R: Manasseh was also given some towns inside the lands of Issachar and Asher. These were Beth-shean, Ibleam, Dor, En-dor, Taanach and Megiddo, with the people who lived in them and the villages around each town. They made up the three hill districts.

decisions.choice: its daughters: the villages that belonged to a town
decisions.reason: A town's "daughters" are the smaller settlements around it that depended on it, as in Numbers 21:25, 32.

decisions.choice: Beth-shean, Ibleam, Dor, En-dor, Taanach, Megiddo: strong Canaanite towns along the valleys
decisions.reason: These towns guarded the Valley of Jezreel and the coastal plain, the main roads across the north of the land. Beth-shean stood where the valley meets the Jordan (verse 16), Megiddo and Taanach on the valley's south-west edge, and Dor on the coast. Though they lay in or beside the land of Issachar and Asher, they were given to Manasseh. Verse 12 says Manasseh could not take them; Judges 1:27 lists the same towns.

decisions.choice: the three of the heights: an unclear phrase, probably naming three hill districts
decisions.reason: The last words are hard to explain. The word may mean "height" or "hill region", and the phrase may refer to three of the towns just named that stood on high ground, or to districts linked with Naphath-dor, the heights of Dor (11:2; 12:23). It could also be read "the third is Napheth", a note on Dor. The rendering keeps the most likely sense.

decisions.choice: the inhabitants of Dor: the people as well as the towns
decisions.reason: From Dor on, the list names "the inhabitants of" each town. The change prepares for verse 12, where those inhabitants, the Canaanites, stay in the land.

decisions.choice: each with its villages
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "with its villages" once for the whole list rather than after every name. Literal keeps the repetition.

source.text: וְלֹ֤א יָכְלוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה לְהוֹרִ֖ישׁ אֶת־הֶֽעָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַיּ֨וֹאֶל֙ הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֔י לָשֶׁ֖בֶת בָּאָ֥רֶץ הַזֹּֽאת׃

records.literal_gloss: And not were able [the] sons of Manasseh to take possession of these cities; and was determined the Canaanite to dwell in this land.

en.L: But the {{gender:descendants|sons}} of Manasseh were not able to take possession of these cities, and the Canaanites were determined to dwell in this land.
en.B: But the descendants of Manasseh could not take over these towns, because the Canaanites were determined to stay in that land.
en.R: But Manasseh's descendants could not take over those towns. The Canaanites refused to leave that part of the land.

decisions.choice: take possession of: take over by driving out those living there
decisions.reason: The verb means to take possession, often by dispossessing the people already there. The tribe was given the towns but could not make them its own (Judges 1:27).

decisions.choice: was determined: set on staying, refused to leave
decisions.reason: The verb means to resolve or be willing to do something. The Canaanites held on and would not give up their land (Judges 1:27, 35).

decisions.choice: the Canaanite: the Canaanites as a people
decisions.reason: The word is singular, "the Canaanite", used for the whole people, as often in lists of nations (Deuteronomy 7:1).

decisions.choice: because
decisions.reason: Balanced joins the two clauses with "because", since the second gives the reason for the first. Literal keeps "and"; Readable uses two sentences.

source.text: וַֽיְהִ֗י כִּ֤י חָֽזְקוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיִּתְּנ֥וּ אֶת־הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֖י לָמַ֑ס וְהוֹרֵ֖שׁ לֹ֥א הוֹרִישֽׁוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when grew strong [the] sons of Israel, and they put the Canaanite to forced labor; and dispossessing not he dispossessed him.

en.L: And it came about, when the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel grew strong, that they put the Canaanites to forced labor, but they did not fully dispossess them.
en.B: Later, when the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} had grown stronger, they made the Canaanites do forced labor, but they never drove them out completely.
en.R: In time the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} became stronger. Then they made the Canaanites work for them as forced laborers. But the Israelites never drove all of them out.

decisions.choice: forced labor: work demanded of a subject people
decisions.reason: The word means a body of forced workers, or the labor they owed. Israel made the Canaanites serve them in this way rather than driving them out, as Deuteronomy 20:11 allowed for a distant city that made peace, but not for the peoples of the land itself (Deuteronomy 20:16-17). Solomon later used such forced workers (1 Kings 9:20-21).

decisions.choice: dispossessing he did not dispossess: they did not drive them out completely
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis, and the negative goes with the whole: they did not carry the work through. The verb and object are singular, "he" and "him", treating Israel and the Canaanites each as one people.

decisions.choice: when Israel grew strong: they could have driven them out but did not
decisions.reason: The verse says the failure was not only weakness. Once Israel was strong enough, it chose to profit from the Canaanites' labor. Judges 1:28 repeats the verse, and Judges 2:1-3 gives the LORD's judgment on it.

decisions.choice: drove them out (B, R); dispossess (L)
decisions.reason: For peoples, Literal says "dispossess" and Balanced and Readable "drive out", the wording used for this verb through Numbers to Ruth.

source.text: וַֽיְדַבְּרוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יוֹסֵ֔ף אֶת־יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ לֵאמֹ֑ר מַדּוּעַ֩ נָתַ֨תָּה לִּ֜י נַחֲלָ֗ה גּוֹרָ֤ל אֶחָד֙ וְחֶ֣בֶל אֶחָ֔ד וַֽאֲנִ֣י עַם־רָ֔ב עַ֥ד אֲשֶׁר־עַד־כֹּ֖ה בֵּֽרְכַ֥נִי יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And spoke [the] sons of Joseph with Joshua, saying, why have you given to me [as] inheritance one lot and one portion, and I [am] a people numerous, inasmuch as until thus has blessed me Yahweh?

en.L: And the {{gender:descendants|sons}} of Joseph spoke to Joshua, saying, "Why have you given me [as] an inheritance one lot and one portion, when I [am] a numerous people, since {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has blessed me so far?"
en.B: Joseph's descendants asked Joshua, "Why have you given us just one allotment, a single share, as our inheritance? We are a large people, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has blessed us until now."
en.R: Joseph's descendants said to Joshua, "Why did you give us only one share of the land? There are so many of us, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has blessed us greatly."

decisions.choice: me, I: the tribes speak as one people
decisions.reason: The descendants of Joseph speak in the singular, "me" and "I", as one people, the house of Joseph (verse 17). The meaning is "us" and "we".

decisions.choice: one lot and one portion: one share for the two tribes of Joseph
decisions.reason: Joseph's sons Ephraim and Manasseh were counted as two tribes (Genesis 48:5), and Manasseh's land has just been described apart from Ephraim's. But it came by a single lot (16:1), and Joseph's descendants complain that it is too small for two large tribes. "Portion" is the measured piece of land, as in verse 5.

decisions.choice: a numerous people whom the LORD has blessed
decisions.reason: Their numbers are the blessing promised to Joseph's sons (Genesis 48:4, 16, 19-20; 49:22). The census counted 52,700 men of Manasseh and 32,500 of Ephraim (Numbers 26:34, 37).

decisions.choice: us, we
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use "us" and "we", as the plural speakers mean (m1). Literal keeps the singular, and Balanced adds "just" to bring out the complaint in "one lot".

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם יְהוֹשֻׁ֗עַ אִם־עַם־רַ֤ב אַתָּה֙ עֲלֵ֣ה לְךָ֣ הַיַּ֔עְרָה וּבֵרֵאתָ֤ לְךָ֙ שָׁ֔ם בְּאֶ֥רֶץ הַפְּרִזִּ֖י וְהָֽרְפָאִ֑ים כִּֽי־אָ֥ץ לְךָ֖ הַר־אֶפְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to them Joshua, if a people numerous [are] you, go up for yourself to the forest and cut down for yourself there in [the] land of the Perizzite and the Rephaim, since is narrow for you [the] hill country of Ephraim.

en.L: And Joshua said to them, "If you [are] a numerous people, go up for yourself to the forest and cut [it] down for yourself there in the land of the Perizzites and the Rephaim, since the hill country of Ephraim is too narrow for you."
en.B: Joshua answered them, "If you are so many, go up into the forest and clear land for yourselves there, in the land of the Perizzites and the Rephaim, since the hill country of Ephraim is too small for you."
en.R: Joshua answered, "If there are so many of you, and the hill country of Ephraim is too small for you, then go up into the forest. Cut down the trees there and make room for yourselves in the land of the Perizzites and the Rephaim."

decisions.choice: cut down: clear forest land to live on
decisions.reason: The verb in this form means to cut down trees and so clear ground (verse 18; Ezekiel 23:47 uses it of cutting down people with swords). Joshua tells them to make room by clearing the wooded hills.

decisions.choice: the Perizzites and the Rephaim: peoples living in the wooded hills
decisions.reason: The Perizzites are one of the peoples of Canaan (3:10; Genesis 13:7). The Rephaim were an ancient people remembered for their great size (Deuteronomy 2:10-11, 20-21; 3:11). The land Joshua points to was still held by such peoples.

decisions.choice: the hill country of Ephraim: the central hills held by the tribes of Joseph
decisions.reason: The name is used for the hill country of central Canaan as a whole, including the part given to Manasseh, not only Ephraim's share (24:30; Judges 4:5). It is "narrow" for them: too small.

decisions.choice: you: the tribes addressed as one
decisions.reason: Joshua answers in the singular, as they spoke (verse 14).

decisions.choice: cut [it] down (L); clear land (B); cut down the trees ... make room (R)
decisions.reason: The verb has no object. Literal brackets "it", the forest; Balanced and Readable say what the clearing was for.

decisions.choice: the reason first
decisions.reason: Readable puts the clause about the small hill country before the command, so the reason comes before the advice.

source.text: וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יוֹסֵ֔ף לֹֽא־יִמָּ֥צֵא לָ֖נוּ הָהָ֑ר וְרֶ֣כֶב בַּרְזֶ֗ל בְּכָל־הַֽכְּנַעֲנִי֙ הַיֹּשֵׁ֣ב בְּאֶֽרֶץ־הָעֵ֔מֶק לַֽאֲשֶׁ֤ר בְּבֵית־שְׁאָן֙ וּבְנוֹתֶ֔יהָ וְלַֽאֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּעֵ֥מֶק יִזְרְעֶֽאל׃

records.literal_gloss: And said [the] sons of Joseph, not will be found for us the hill country, and chariotry of iron [is] among all the Canaanite who dwells in [the] land of the valley, to [those] who [are] in Beth-shean and its daughters and to [those] who [are] in [the] valley of Jezreel.

en.L: And the {{gender:descendants|sons}} of Joseph said, "The hill country will not be enough for us, and iron chariots [are] among all the Canaanites who dwell in the land of the valley, both those who [are] in Beth-shean and its villages and those who [are] in the valley of Jezreel."
en.B: The descendants of Joseph replied, "The hill country is too small for us, and the Canaanites who live down in the valley all have iron chariots, both those in Beth-shean and its villages and those in the Valley of Jezreel."
en.R: Joseph's descendants answered, "The hill country is not big enough for us. But all the Canaanites living in the valley below have chariots made with iron. That includes the people of Beth-shean and its villages and the people in the Valley of Jezreel."

decisions.choice: will not be found for us: will not be enough for us
decisions.reason: The verb "be found" here means to be at hand or enough, as in Numbers 11:22. The hill country will not hold them all.

decisions.choice: iron chariots: war chariots fitted with iron
decisions.reason: These were horse-drawn war chariots, probably made of wood with iron fittings, or with iron parts in the wheels and frame. On the flat ground of the valleys they made the Canaanites hard to defeat, while in the wooded hills they were of little use (Judges 1:19; 4:3).

decisions.choice: the valley, Beth-shean, the Valley of Jezreel: the wide plain across the north
decisions.reason: The Valley of Jezreel runs from the coast inland to Beth-shean by the Jordan. It was rich farmland and the main road across the land, held by Canaanite towns (verse 11).

decisions.choice: chariots made with iron
decisions.reason: Readable says the chariots were made with iron, without claiming they were iron through and through (m2).

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ית יוֹסֵ֔ף לְאֶפְרַ֥יִם וְלִמְנַשֶּׁ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר עַם־רַ֣ב אַתָּ֗ה וְכֹ֤חַ גָּדוֹל֙ לָ֔ךְ לֹֽא־יִהְיֶ֥ה לְךָ֖ גּוֹרָ֥ל אֶחָֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Joshua to [the] house of Joseph, to Ephraim and to Manasseh, saying, a people numerous [are] you and strength great [is] to you; not will be to you a lot one,

en.L: And Joshua said to the house of Joseph, to Ephraim and to Manasseh, saying, "You [are] a numerous people, and you have great strength; you shall not have one lot [only],
en.B: Then Joshua answered the house of Joseph, Ephraim and Manasseh: "You are a large people and you have great strength. You will not have just one allotment,
en.R: Joshua said to Joseph's descendants, the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh, "There are many of you, and you are very strong. So you will not have only one share of land.

decisions.choice: the house of Joseph: the two tribes descended from Joseph
decisions.reason: "House" here means a family line. Joshua names the two tribes, Ephraim and Manasseh, so it is clear his answer is for both.

decisions.choice: a numerous people with great strength: their claim turned into a charge
decisions.reason: Joshua takes up their own words (verse 14). If they are many and strong, they can win more land for themselves; their size is a reason to act, not to complain.

decisions.choice: you shall not have one lot: you will have more than a single share
decisions.reason: Joshua grants their request: their land will not be limited to the one lot. Verse 18 says how: by clearing the forested hill country and driving out the Canaanites.

decisions.choice: one lot [only] (L); just one allotment (B)
decisions.reason: The sense is "not one lot only"; Literal brackets "only" and Balanced says "just". The sentence runs on into verse 18 at Literal and Balanced.

source.text: כִּ֣י הַ֤ר יִֽהְיֶה־לָּךְ֙ כִּֽי־יַ֣עַר ה֔וּא וּבֵ֣רֵאת֔וֹ וְהָיָ֥ה לְךָ֖ תֹּֽצְאֹתָ֑יו כִּֽי־תוֹרִ֣ישׁ אֶת־הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֗י כִּ֣י רֶ֤כֶב בַּרְזֶל֙ ל֔וֹ כִּ֥י חָזָ֖ק הֽוּא׃פ

records.literal_gloss: for hill country will be to you, for forest it [is], and you will cut it down, and will be to you its goings out; for you will dispossess the Canaanite, though chariotry of iron [is] to him, though strong he [is].

en.L: for the hill country will be yours; for it [is] a forest, and you will cut it down, and its farthest reaches will be yours; for you will dispossess the Canaanites, though they have iron chariots, though they [are] strong."
en.B: but the hill country will be yours as well. It is forest, but you will clear it, and it will be yours to its farthest edges. You will drive out the Canaanites, even though they have iron chariots and are strong."
en.R: The hill country will be yours too. It is covered with forest, but you will clear it, and all of it will be yours. And you will drive out the Canaanites, even though they have iron chariots and are strong."

decisions.choice: the hill country will be yours: the forested hills of verse 15
decisions.reason: "Hill country" here has no article. It means the wooded high ground Joshua spoke of in verse 15, which is to be theirs as well as the land already given.

decisions.choice: its goings out: its farthest limits
decisions.reason: As in verse 9, the word means the farthest point land reaches. Here it means the forest land will be theirs to its very edges, perhaps including the valleys below.

decisions.choice: though ... though: the Canaanites' strength does not stop them
decisions.reason: The word that usually means "for" or "because" can also mean "though". In the last two clauses it most likely means "though": Israel will drive them out despite their chariots and strength. The last clause could also be read as a reason, "because they are strong", the reason Israel must drive them out rather than live beside them.

decisions.choice: the Canaanite, he: the Canaanites as one people
decisions.reason: As in verses 12-13, the people are named in the singular. Their chariots and strength answer the fear Joseph's descendants voiced in verse 16.

decisions.choice: they
decisions.reason: Every level says "the Canaanites" and "they" for the singular "the Canaanite" and "he", since the people as a whole is meant (m4). The literal gloss keeps the singular.

decisions.choice: drive out (B, R); dispossess (L)
decisions.reason: As in verse 13.
